messages:
carmen: Heads up — CI is red on my branch feature/epoch-ops after a rebase onto main. Failing 3 tests in runtime/shard_allocator affinity. I can reproduce locally but only on the ubuntu-20 runner. I pushed a debug build to the PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/412
liam: sorry about that, looking now. which commit did you rebase onto?
maya: ping me if you want a quick rerun on dedicated infra, I have spare quota. :wave:
ci-bot: [job: run/84219] job started by carmen — ubuntu-20 / shard-allocator-tests
ci-bot: [job: run/84219] failing tests: 3 (shard_affinity_test::alloc_race, shard_affinity_test::evict_order, shard_cache_test::flush_race)
carmen: rebased onto main@2f9c6b1 (merged yesterday). Locally `./bazel test //runtime/shard:shard_affinity_test` fails 2/3 times. Logs attached in PR comment.
liam: can you paste the failing stack snippet? sometimes the order differs after the allocator change.
carmen: here — stack trace from CI:
```
runtime::shard::Allocator::allocate() at allocator.cc:214
runtime::shard::EvictQueue::pop() at evict.cc:89
runtime::cache::FlushWorker::run() at flush.cc:47
Assertion failed: eviction list not empty
```
maya: hmm looks like a timing-sensitive race. My guess: kernel/jemalloc change in main altered free timing. Two quick options: (1) rerun the flaky shard CI with isolated seed, (2) bisect the rebase range to find offending commit.
liam: agree. Carmen — could you try `bazel test //runtime/shard:shard_affinity_test --runs_per_test=10` and see failure frequency? If low, we can rerun CI a few times. If high, bisect.
carmen: running now, will post results.
ci-bot: [job: run/84219] test output snippet:
```
[ RUN      ] shard_affinity_test.alloc_race
[       OK ] shard_affinity_test.alloc_race (123 ms)
[ RUN      ] shard_affinity_test.evict_order
[  FAILED  ] shard_affinity_test.evict_order (67 ms)
[ RUN      ] shard_cache_test.flush_race
[  FAILED  ] shard_cache_test.flush_race (40 ms)
```
carmen: local runs: 10 runs -> 3 failures (evict_order x2, flush_race x1). I'll try rerunning CI once to see if it clears.
maya: if CI rerun helps, we should still open a small flaky-investigation ticket pointing to the allocator timelines; I'll file one and add steps to repro.
liam: if you want to bisect, start with `git bisect start main HEAD -- template` — I can throw together a bisect script that runs the test and exits non-zero on failure. Up to you.
carmen: ok I kicked off a CI rerun: https://ci.redwood-inference/run/84220 — tagging @maya for infra rerun if it flakes again. :crossed_fingers:
ci-bot: [job: run/84220] rerun started by carmen
ci-bot: [job: run/84220] final: job still failing — same two tests failing (evict_order, flush_race)
maya: thanks — I'll provision a dedicated runner and rerun with `--runs_per_test=50` to get stable stats. Give me 15m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
liam: meanwhile I skimmed the rebase diff; there's a small change in allocator free ordering in commit 2e8b4a3 that looks suspicious. If bisect confirms, we can revert or patch ordering.
carmen: updated PR with bisect instruction + temporary flaky skip for the two tests (skips are guarded under an env var). Putting this in draft until we have a fix.
maya: created infra run: https://ci.redwood-inference/run/84302 (dedicated runner, 50 iterations). I'll post results when done.
liam: thanks all. If infra run shows >5% failure, we should prioritize a fix. Otherwise mark as flaky and proceed with revert candidate. :thumbsup:
